# simplevm_volume_attachment (Resource)

Attaches a SimpleVM volume to a VM.

Attaching and detaching are asynchronous: the provider polls SimpleVM until the volume is `in-use` (attach) or `available` (detach); see `timeouts`. Both arguments replace the attachment when changed.

If the volume or the VM is deleted outside Terraform, or the volume is detached outside Terraform, the attachment is removed from state on the next refresh. Destroying an attachment whose VM is already gone does nothing, since SimpleVM detaches volumes when deleting a VM.

The `attach` and `detach` request shapes are assumed from the SimpleVM wiki.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "simplevm_volume_attachment" "data" {
  volume_id = simplevm_volume.data.id
  vm_id     = simplevm_vm.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vm_id` (String) UUID of the VM to attach the volume to. Changing it replaces the attachment.
- `volume_id` (String) UUID of the volume to attach. Changing it replaces the attachment.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) Timeouts for long-running operations, as Go durations such as `30m` or `1h`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `device` (String) Device name inside the VM, for example `/dev/vdb`.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the attachment, `<volume_id>/<vm_id>`.
- `path` (String) Mount path of the volume as reported by SimpleVM.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Timeout for the create operation (default `10m`). A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) Timeout for the delete operation (default `10m`). A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An attachment is imported as <volume_uuid>/<vm_uuid>.
terraform import simplevm_volume_attachment.data 3f2a9c4e-1b7d-4e8a-9c21-5d6f7a8b9c0d/7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
```
